question: Which bone forms the large, flared upper part of the hip bone?
explanation: The ilium is the broad, upper fan-shaped section of the hip bone that you feel on your waist. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h1)

question: What do we call the joint right at the front where the pubic bones meet?
explanation: Great job! The pubic symphysis is simply the cartilaginous joint joining the right and left pubic bones right at the front midline. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h2)

question: Why do a pregnant woman's pelvic ligaments loosen up?

options.A: To prevent pressure on the urinary bladder
options.B: To compensate for weaker leg muscles
options.C: To allow increased movement for childbirth

explanation: Nature is amazing! Hormones soften these ligaments during pregnancy so the pelvis can stretch and help the baby pass through easily. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which part of the pelvis serves as the actual passageway for a baby during birth?
explanation: Spot on! The true pelvis is the lower bony canal that the baby travels through during delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the boundary line that separates the false pelvis from the true pelvis?
explanation: Think of the pelvic brim as the dividing line sitting right between the upper false pelvis and the lower true pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the name of the upper opening into the true pelvis?
explanation: You're doing great! The pelvic inlet is literally the 'entrance' or upper opening where the baby first enters the true pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h4)

question: As a midwife checking the lower boundary of the pelvic cavity, which bones help form the pelvic outlet?
explanation: Think of the bottom exit of the pelvis: it's bounded by your tailbone (coccyx), the sitting bones (ischial tuberosities), and the front pubic bone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which pelvic shape is the best and most normal for a smooth vaginal delivery?
explanation: The gynecoid pelvis is the classic female shape—nice, rounded, and roomy, making it ideal for childbirth! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h5)

question: What makes an 'android' pelvis shape stand out?

options.A: It is heart-shaped with prominent ischial spines
options.B: It is narrow and oval with a very long front-to-back measurement
options.C: It is flat and wide with a short front-to-back diameter
options.D: It is a classic round shape found in most females

explanation: An android pelvis is more like a male pelvis, featuring a heart-shaped opening that can sometimes make labor a bit tricky. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which of these features is typically seen in a female pelvis rather than a male pelvis?
explanation: Women have a nice wide pubic arch to help make room for a baby to pass through easily. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h6)

question: Why is the male pelvis typically narrower and deeper than the female pelvis?

options.A: It is designed to hold more abdominal fat and organs
options.B: It protects the spinal cord from compression during heavy lifting
options.C: It allows for faster walking and running speeds
options.D: It is built for greater overall physical strength and leverage

explanation: Male pelvic bones are built heavier and narrower to support greater muscle strength and heavy physical work, rather than childbearing. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h6)

question: What do we call the medical measurement of the inside of a woman's pelvis to check if she can deliver vaginally?
explanation: You've got this! Pelvimetry is just measuring the birth canal dimensions to make sure everything can fit safely. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is it called when a baby's head is simply too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?
explanation: Don't let the big words scare you: 'cephalic' means head, 'pelvic' means pelvis, and 'disproportion' means a size mismatch between the two! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h7)
